subject: general
question: A tower stands vertically on the ground. From a point on the ground which is 27.6 m away from the foot of the tower, the angle of elevation of the top of the tower is found to be 45°. Find the height of the tower.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the **angle of elevation** is 45°, the **height** of the tower and its **base distance** (shadow) are always equal because tan 45° = 1.

Ratio of Height : Base = 1 : 1

Since the base distance is 27.6 m, the height must also be 27.6 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 27.6 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/648dfe8c991bd7ae2e558eb105cee8b45caf97ceb0d9b80ddc79ed71487f6ed7.png] 

**Given:**

Distance from foot (Base) = 27.6 m

Angle of elevation (θ) = 45°

**Formula Used:**

tan θ = Perpendicular (Height) ÷ Base

**Calculations:**

⇒ tan 45° = Height ÷ 27.6

⇒ 1 = Height ÷ 27.6

⇒ Height = 27.6 × 1

⇒ Height = 27.6 m

**∴ The correct answer is 27.6 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios for Standard Angles

tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, and tan 60° = √3. These are frequently used in height and distance problems.

Special Right Triangle (45-45-90)

In a 45°−45°−90° triangle, the legs are equal in length, and the hypotenuse is leg × √2.

Angle of Elevation vs Depression

The angle of elevation from an observer's eye to an object is numerically equal to the angle of depression from the object to the observer's eye due to alternate interior angles.</p
